input_domain: Sealed generated PDF 1.7 candidates with an independently pinned page-window plan
license_notice: Existing THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt and parser dependency notices remain required
text_normalization: None; preserve extracted Unicode and UTF-8 bytes, including physical line breaks

process_profile.launch: isolated Python with explicit worker path
process_profile.protocol_storage: two inherited distinct anonymous regular file descriptors

known_issues: The parser reads global PDF structures to resolve pages; only the selected text interval is inspected. This is not whole-document object, tag, metadata, link, font, raster or accessibility validation.
PDF parsing and content decompression may allocate memory before Python-level size checks; fixed process memory/CPU/wall bounds remain mandatory.
Every selected page must contain nonempty extractable text. Image-only or blank pages are rejected rather than silently skipped or OCR-processed.
This profile does not establish equivalence between extracted text and the sealed scientific or presentation source.
A receipt contains unsigned counts and hashes, not transferable worker, job or storage authentication. The caller must preserve trusted execution provenance.
The fixed per-invocation budget does not bound all windows, repeated parsing, parent-side input preparation, scheduling, storage or total-job resources.
The 512-page internal admission class and 16-page window size are finite execution constraints, not an editorial truncation rule or final long-document release qualification.
The default whole-file 32-page and 8-MiB limits remain unchanged; a successful window must never replace those checks or authorize report delivery.
Existing process-local guard limitations, inherited protocol descriptors and startup-before-registration constraints remain explicit. Unsupported confinement fails without a fallback.
disable_path: Leave this opt-in adapter unused; retain downstream whole-document and release gates
